Definition: from κάρφω (to wither); a dry twig or straw:--mote.
BiblicalUsage: Karphos is the mote — the dry twig, the speck of straw in a brother's eye. Why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother's eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother's eye.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the mote is the test of my sight: if I can see the speck in my brother's eye but not the beam in my own, I am blind — and the first surgery is always on myself. Clear sight begins at home.
